sections.html:
On the North Shore of Essex County, 17 miles northeast of Boston, Beverly had 42,670 residents and 17,887 housing units in 2020, with 4.9 percent vacant. About a third of its 22.6 square miles is water.

The western half is more built up, and the eastern half, from Woodbury Point eastward, is more rural. Residents name these areas most often:

  • Ryal Side
  • North Beverly
  • Centerville
  • Cove
  • Montserrat
  • Beverly Farms and Prides Crossing

Coast, harbor and river make street-level location matter, so a pair of houses a few miles apart can sell very differently.

Route 128 crosses Beverly from east to west and connects to Interstate 95 and Route 1 in Peabody. Route 1A runs north and south through downtown. Beverly is where the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport and Rockport lines split, and it has more commuter rail stations than any other Massachusetts municipality except Boston.

  • Beverly Depot, near downtown, served by both lines
  • North Beverly, on the Newburyport line
  • Montserrat and Beverly Farms, on the Rockport line

Service to Prides Crossing station is suspended indefinitely. Beyond the trains, buyers look at Lynch Park and its beaches in the Cove section, downtown with its two historic theaters, and employers such as Beverly Hospital, Endicott College and Axcelis Technologies.

sections.h2: Places that help a Beverly listing
sections.html:
Beverly has history and waterfront that buyers respond to, and it helps to know the talking points. Lynch Park in the Cove section is the main public park, a popular summer spot for swimming and kayaking. The city has five beaches and two yacht clubs, Jubilee Yacht Club in Beverly Harbor and Bass Haven Yacht Club on the Bass River. Downtown has the Cabot, reopened as a nonprofit performing arts center in 2014, and the Larcom Theatre, which dates to 1912.

The city was settled in 1626, set off from Salem as a town in 1668 and became a city in 1894. That long history means houses vary widely in age. Older ones often need updated wiring, heating or roofing, and buyers using a mortgage may ask for those repairs. The former United Shoe Machinery complex is now a campus of offices, medical practices, shops and restaurants, and its presence keeps nearby commercial activity steady.

If your house is near a station or the water, say so. If it is on the more rural eastern side, mention the lot and whether it is on septic.

Expect about 48 inches of precipitation and 51 inches of snow in a year, with the heaviest snow in January and February. Thunderstorms, summer tropical rain and cooler-season nor'easters all come through, and houses near the harbor, the Bass River or the coves take more of that weather than houses inland. Inspectors for buyers will look hard at the roof, gutters and basement.

The Beverly Assessors set values for 13,037 real estate parcels and 1,551 personal property accounts as of January 1 each year. For fiscal 2026 the residential tax rate is $10.81 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the commercial rate is $20.98. Rates are reset each fiscal year.

The assessing office also reviews building permits to see how they change a property's value, so a renovation can raise the next assessment. It posts a fiscal 2026 abatement application, exemption guides for seniors, service members and others, and a deferral application.

AssessorsCity Hall, 191 Cabot Street978-605-2307

The state's Appellate Tax Board guide sets the rule: an abatement application must reach the assessors by the due date of the first actual tax bill. In towns that bill quarterly that is generally February 1. Call the Beverly collector to find out which schedule applies to you, and keep paying your installments while the application is pending.

At closing your deed goes on record at the Southern Essex District Registry of Deeds. Fees follow the registry's own schedule, so your closing attorney can quote the current excise tax and recording charges.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. A sale needs a certificate of compliance from the city fire department. Phone once the closing date is fixed, and budget for an inspection fee.
  • Septic, if any. The eastern part of Beverly is more rural. If the house has a septic system, plan on a Title 5 inspection, done in the two years before the sale or in the six months after when weather interferes.
  • Attorney. When a lender is involved, an attorney has to take a real part in the closing, so hire one early.

Most land in the state is recorded at the Registry of Deeds. A minority is registered land, backed by a Land Court certificate of title.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you sell
sections.html:
1. Pull your latest tax bill and mark which installments are still open.
  2. Call the assessor's line, 978-605-2307, to confirm your assessed value and whether an abatement or exemption is on file.
  3. Find out whether the house is on sewer or septic, and book the Title 5 inspection if septic.
  4. Schedule the fire department alarm certificate when a closing date is set.
  5. Download the recent sales list the assessors post and see what comparable houses brought.
  6. Gather your mortgage statement, if any, so your attorney can confirm the payoff before closing.

Renovations deserve a note. The assessing office reviews building permits, so recent work may already show in your value. Keep the permits in one folder, because a buyer's attorney may want them.

sections.h2: If you owe taxes or carry a lien
sections.html: Owing tax does not block a sale. At closing the payoff is taken from your proceeds, and your attorney needs the exact figure for that day. Get the balance from the Beverly collector, learn from the assessors whether an exemption or deferral changes it, and hand both answers to your attorney. Do it before accepting any offer, so the net number you compare is real.

Deciding between a listing and a direct sale? Put the posted recent sales next to an offer. Cash Home Buyers buys Beverly houses as they are, so there are no repairs or showings, and you can set our figure against a listing price. Count repair costs, carrying costs while a listing waits for a buyer, and any tax payoff.

A direct sale fits a vacant house, one needing septic work, or one from an estate. A listing may earn more for a polished house on a sought-after street. Both routes still end with a tax payoff, an alarm certificate and a recorded deed.

faqs.q: What county is Beverly, MA in?
faqs.a: Essex County. Beverly is a North Shore city about 17 miles northeast of Boston, and its deeds are recorded at the Southern Essex District Registry of Deeds.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Beverly?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the residential rate is $10.81 per $1,000 of assessed value and the commercial rate is $20.98. Rates are reset each fiscal year.

faqs.q: How many neighborhoods does Beverly have?
faqs.a: Residents name Ryal Side, North Beverly, Centerville, Cove, Montserrat, Beverly Farms and Prides Crossing. These are named areas rather than legal districts.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell in Beverly?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet sale requirements. The department charges a fee.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to contest a Beverly assessment?
faqs.a: An abatement application must reach the assessors by the due date of the first actual tax bill, generally February 1 in quarterly billing towns. Call the assessor at 978-605-2307 to confirm.
